purpose: Postmortem for the remote CPU 'big sweep' that trained and ranked no-insider dense probe candidates for Qwen answer-token pooled features.

false_positive_thread.reason: It also contained the phrase 'big sweep' but was a June 3 PR review session and unrelated to this remote CPU sweep.

achieved_in_this_postmortem.limiting_condition: The multi-agent tool hit an agent thread limit before the full requested 10 x 5 fanout could be created.

executive_summary.outcome: Success: 182 expected probe-training JSON results were produced and summarized with no final duplicate active writers and no critical log signatures.
executive_summary.best_candidate_interpretation: The best ranked setting excluded the REPE honesty task, used layer 21, and used strong regularization C=0.01.
executive_summary.infrastructure_result: The final path used a local dense pooled-feature cache, uploaded the 11.19 GB cache to a 48-logical-CPU Latitude host, then ran many single-core liblinear jobs in parallel.
executive_summary.main_speed_win: The decisive optimization was switching away from a 62.39 GB raw HDF5 upload and remote feature extraction toward an 11.19 GB dense pooled cache and cache-only training.
executive_summary.main_risk: Manual launcher/filler orchestration briefly created duplicate starts when lock names were seeded with the wrong suffix. The issue was caught and corrected before the final monitored state.
executive_summary.largest_remaining_unknown: The run proved high CPU occupancy but did not collect enough iostat/mpstat/per-job telemetry to precisely separate CPU, memory bandwidth, and disk effects.

remote.label: Latitude c3.large.x86 class host
remote.trust_note: A later live SSH attempt saw a changed host key; the current IP should not be assumed to be the same server.

local_comparison.comparison: Remote had about 2.7x as many logical CPUs and about 3.9x as much RAM. Running 47-48 one-process-per-job fits locally would not be a like-for-like option without more aggressive memory throttling.

abandoned_raw_hdf5_route.reason_abandoned: The raw upload was much larger and slow; cache-only training avoided moving and reprocessing unnecessary data.

inputs_and_grid.grid_formula: 13 layers x 7 C values x 2 task sets = 182 jobs

model_training.process_parallelism: Parallelism came from many independent Python processes, not from sklearn n_jobs.

tail_159_to_182.interpretation: Tail throughput stayed reasonable until the final few long high-C jobs; the last 2-to-1 active drain was inherently hard to parallelize.

interpretation.claim: The top-ranked candidates are concentrated around layers 19-23 and low C values.
The no_repe task set dominated the top ranks.
The all_no_insider task set remained competitive but its first appearance in the shown ranking was below multiple no_repe candidates.

caveats: No sustained mpstat, iostat, perf, or per-job memory trace was captured.
The final drain could not keep 48 CPUs occupied because only one or two long jobs remained.

notes: The $1.36/hr value came from the dashboard/session context, not a current public price lookup.
Actual billing should be checked against Latitude billing records if exact cost matters.

what_went_well.detail: Building and uploading the dense pooled cache cut transfer volume from 62.39 GB to 11.19 GB and avoided remote feature extraction.
liblinear jobs were single-core-ish and process-isolated, so many independent jobs could occupy the 48 logical CPUs.
The controller required all 182 expected outputs, no active jobs, no lock/plain missing states, no duplicate active outputs, and no critical signatures before finishing.

failures_or_near_misses.detail: A 62.39 GB raw HDF5 upload was started before the dense-cache route became canonical.
Earlier setup saw errors such as missing h5py and rsync code 12. They did not affect the final cache-backed sweep.

failures_or_near_misses.item: Lock seeding bug during manual acceleration
failures_or_near_misses.detail: Manual lock dirs were initially seeded with a .json suffix while the runner expected lock names without .json, briefly starting duplicate layer-22 jobs. The launcher was paused, duplicates corrected, and final monitor later reported dup=0.
The cache fast path coordinator emitted an unexpected EOF after the cache had already assembled, verified, and started the runner.

failures_or_near_misses.item: No durable structured run-control plan id
failures_or_near_misses.detail: The final run used shell scripts, tmux sessions, and lock dirs rather than a structured queue_plan or plan_id that would make replay and auditing cleaner.

efficiency_left_on_table.expected_benefit: Avoid manual tmux/filler orchestration and duplicate-lock edge cases.
efficiency_left_on_table.specific_change: Represent the 182 jobs in a manifest with unique output ids, launch through a bounded worker pool, and persist state transitions to sqlite/jsonl.

efficiency_left_on_table.expected_benefit: Save the time spent on the 62.39 GB raw upload path.
efficiency_left_on_table.specific_change: Make dense-cache feasibility the default preflight for this class of sweep.

efficiency_left_on_table.expected_benefit: Reduce tail time by starting historically slow high-C/later-layer jobs earlier.
efficiency_left_on_table.specific_change: Sort jobs by predicted runtime before dispatch, using previous per-layer/C timings.

efficiency_left_on_table.expected_benefit: Separate CPU, RAM, disk, and Python overhead instead of inferring from active count and load.
efficiency_left_on_table.specific_change: Collect mpstat, iostat, per-job wall/user/sys time, peak RSS, and result-write time.

efficiency_left_on_table.expected_benefit: Possible speedups or lower memory pressure, but requires validation.
efficiency_left_on_table.specific_change: Benchmark liblinear vs saga/lbfgs, float32 feature matrices, memory mapping, and BLIS/VECLIB/threadpoolctl caps on a small artifact before full sweeps.

efficiency_left_on_table.expected_benefit: A 64-96 logical CPU host may shorten wall time if memory bandwidth and RAM scale with cores.
efficiency_left_on_table.specific_change: Run a 20-job benchmark on candidate SKUs and optimize cost per completed job rather than hourly price alone.

future_run_playbook.name: Local smoke and cache validation
future_run_playbook.details: Build the minimal dense cache, validate sha256 and schema, and run 1-2 probe jobs from cache before renting a larger host.

future_run_playbook.name: Remote host selection
future_run_playbook.details: Pick CPU host based on logical CPUs, RAM per worker, NVMe space, network ingress, and $/completed-job from prior benchmark.

future_run_playbook.name: Manifested queue
future_run_playbook.details: Generate an explicit job manifest for layer, C, task_set, output path, expected input sha, and estimated duration.

future_run_playbook.name: Bounded worker executor
future_run_playbook.details: Run a single controller that owns scheduling and locking; avoid independent launchers unless they share the same manifest state.

future_run_playbook.name: Continuous telemetry
future_run_playbook.details: Sample active jobs, load, MemAvailable, per-job RSS, iostat, mpstat, and duplicate output claims every 30-60 seconds.

future_run_playbook.name: Final contract
future_run_playbook.details: Do not declare success until expected_count matches, all outputs parse, summary ranking is regenerated, duplicate active count is zero, critical signature count is zero, and the best result file is inspected.

fact_table.claim: The final sweep had 182 expected outputs.
The final summary ranking selected no_repe_layer21_c001 as rank 1.
The dense cache size was 11186928745 bytes and sha256 was 8bfc57d8f74cdc687f3f8e73720479c585bac6f16b72ce6e2bcd18fb5245ad77.
The remote CPU had 48 logical CPUs.
The run achieved peak active process counts of 47-48 on a 48 logical CPU host.
Disk saturation was not measured directly.
evidence_refs: absence of iostat/perf telemetry in reviewed evidence
